title: Asynchronous Vertical Federated Learning for Kernelized AUC Maximization

problem.claim: Vertical federated learning must handle both imbalanced data, which challenges accuracy-based training, and imbalanced computational resources, which complicates synchronous training.

gap.claim: Existing vertical federated learning algorithms primarily focus on accuracy, while synchronous methods are difficult to apply when computational resources are imbalanced.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Asynchronous Vertical Federated Kernelized AUC Maximization (AVFKAM) to address the double imbalance issue.
AVFKAM asynchronously updates a kernel model using triply stochastic gradients for pairwise loss and random feature approximation.
The method transfers coefficient asynchrony to the functional gradient through a dual relationship between model coefficients and the objective function to facilitate theoretical analysis.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AVFKAM converges to the optimal solution at a rate of O(1/t), where t is the global iteration number.
The authors report experimental results on various benchmark datasets showing high AUC performance and efficiency.
The authors discuss the security of the model.

narrative_sequence.summary: Vertical federated learning is motivated by multi-party collaboration and privacy preservation.
Accuracy-focused methods face difficulty with imbalanced data, and synchronous methods face difficulty with imbalanced computational resources.
The authors propose AVFKAM, which asynchronously updates a kernel model using triply stochastic gradients and uses a dual relationship for analysis.
The abstract reports convergence to the optimal solution at rate O(1/t) and discusses model security.
Experiments on various benchmark datasets are reported to show high AUC performance and efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The method targets both label or data imbalance and computational-resource imbalance in federated learning.

interpretation.claim: Optimization objectives and system scheduling may need to be designed jointly when statistical and resource heterogeneity interact.

application.claim: For privacy-preserving collaborative learning with imbalanced labels and heterogeneous clients, consider imbalance-aware metrics together with asynchronous coordination.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the approach generalizes beyond the reported benchmark datasets or resource conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baselines, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not state the assumptions or proof details underlying the O(1/t) convergence rate.
The abstract does not describe the security model or provide security verification details.
